1bit engine: local LLMs on the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395#

Boot a USB stick, and your Strix Halo machine serves local LLMs on its GPU and NPU through AMD's Lemonade Server. That is the whole setup.

Get started#

  1. Download 1bit-os-<version>.img.zst from the releases page.
  2. Write it to a USB stick (8 GB or more).
  3. Boot the machine from the stick. Secure Boot can stay on; the image is signed.
  4. Lemonade comes up with its catalog and web UI. Try it from the live session; to keep it, run 1bit-install <disk> --yes there and the 1bit appliance is on the disk (os/v2/README.md).

Already running Lemonade on Ubuntu? The lemonade-onebit package from the same releases page adds the engine as a Lemonade backend; nothing else changes (Lemonade).

What it is#

The 1bit engine is Lemonade's onebit backend for the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo). It runs the Radeon 8060S iGPU through HRX with our own HIP kernels, and the XDNA 2 NPU through our own NPU runtime, behind the OpenAI-compatible API Lemonade already gives you. Every model is checked on the hardware before it ships; the models and their measured numbers are one page: Models measured.

Milestones#

when what
2026-10-04 The engine becomes HRX + our HIP kernels + the NPU engine, embedded in Lemonade; Vulkan, ROCm and CUDA builds removed (RFC #213, #306)
2026-10-20 One HTTP hop from Lemonade to the engine's server; the stock Ubuntu lemond runs the engine with no patch (#475, #483)
2026-10-21 Every HRX pin change passes a hardware gate on Strix Halo before merge; Qwen3.8-27B decodes at 36 tok/s with MTP on our kernels (#478, Hardware gate)
2026-10-23 First release candidate built, booted from USB on the hardware with Secure Boot on (Releases)
2026-10-25 Microsoft BitNet b1.58 (TQ1_0 / TQ2_0) runs fully on HRX (Models measured)
2026-10-30 The HRX pin carries the DeepSeek-V4.1 port; ONNX Runtime runs in-process with our own execution provider on the NPU; the NPU and the GPU are measured running at the same time (#672, #647, Hybrid)

The release goes out when every item on the release checklist is done (Releases); the weekly Lemonade pin moves with Lemonade's releases.

License#

The source code in this repository is Apache-2.0. See LICENSE.

The release binaries (the Linux package and 1bit OS) also contain two proprietary components, compiled in: the 1bit NPU runtime and the 1bit HIP kernels for HRX. They are not in this repository, their source is not published, and they are not under Apache-2.0: they ship under the 1bit Binary License (free to use for any purpose and to pass on unmodified; third-party parts in NOTICE-BINARY). A build from this repository without them has no NPU engine and runs HRX on the public kernels only (NOTICE, Releases).

How to credit#

Credit is welcome and, for the code, required: the Apache-2.0 license keeps the copyright notices and the NOTICE file with every copy. Three lines are enough:

1bit engine - https://github.com/1bit-MONSTER/engine - Copyright 2026 bong-water-water-bong - Apache-2.0

CITATION.cff carries the same in citation form (GitHub shows it under "Cite this repository"). If you build on a specific piece, name the file or the pull request it came from; the history is public.

Thank you#

Osmantic / ODS comes first. ODS introduced me to vibecoding, and that is where all of this started. Without it, this engine would not exist.

The Lemonade team and AMD's developers. Lemonade is where this engine runs. AMD's developers left breadcrumbs all over the place: the XDNA driver and XRT, IRON and Peano, HRX, their tested llama.cpp integration, their issues, their examples. This engine is what following those breadcrumbs built.

The repositories this engine is built on, in order of importance:

# Repository What it gives this engine License
1 amd/xdna-driver The XDNA 2 NPU kernel driver (amdxdna) the NPU engine runs on GPL-2.0 (driver)
2 Xilinx/XRT AMD's NPU runtime and its API, where the engine's NPU work started Apache-2.0 (userspace)
3 Xilinx/mlir-aie IRON and aiecc: how our own NPU kernels are written and compiled Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
4 Xilinx/llvm-aie Peano, the C++ compiler for the NPU's AI Engine cores Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
5 ggml-org/llama.cpp GGUF inference on the Radeon iGPU through HRX (AMD's tested pair), and on the CPU MIT
6 ROCm/hrx-system (our fork 1bit-MONSTER/hrx-system carries two commits) HRX, AMD's HIP Runtime Extended, behind the HRX0 device
7 torvalds/linux The kernel, with amdxdna and amdgpu in-tree GPL-2.0 WITH Linux-syscall-note
8 huggingface/tokenizers Every model's tokenizer.json, byte-exact, behind our C ABI Apache-2.0
9 NandhaKishorM/laya The router that decides where each request runs Apache-2.0
10 ROCm/FastFlowLM The Q4NX NPU model format and its models on Hugging Face (FastFlowLM/*-NPU2), which the engine's NPU route runs on its own kernels MIT
11 antirez/ds4 (DwarfStar) DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.x and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on its own kernels (ROCm on Strix Halo, CUDA, Metal) MIT

Also built on nlohmann/json (MIT) and yhirose/cpp-httplib (MIT).

Every third-party copyright and license is listed in NOTICE. Each project keeps its own license; nothing here relicenses anyone's work.
